title: Stateful affinity batching sensitivity — internal benchmark draft
body:
Purpose:
This note documents a focused set of microbenchmarks exploring how stateful session affinity (sticky-routing + local KV cache reuse) interacts with batching strategies and model quantization choices. Goal: quantify per-session latency and cost tradeoffs for a mixed workload of short chats (2–6 turns) and long chats (20–120 turns) under three deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).

Background / why this matters (short):
- Customers with interactive experiences care about tail latency and predictable per-session cost.
- Affinity (pinning a session to a worker) improves KV cache hit rate but reduces batching opportunities across sessions.
- We need concrete numbers to drive routing policy defaults and suggested autoscaler profiles in Console.

Benchmarks overview (setup):
- Models: redwood-7B-fp16, redwood-14B-int8 (approx quantized), and a compact redwood-4B-opt.
- Hardware: GPU-A (A100 40GB) representing dedicated; GPU-B (H100) for private testbeds; hosted runs on mixed cloud (autoscaled instances).
- Workload: synthetic mix: 70% short chats (mean 4 turns, 30 tokens/turn), 30% long chats (mean 60 turns, 30 tokens/turn).
- Session arrival process: Poisson with peak QPS = 320, off-peak = 40.
- Policies tested:
  * No-affinity opportunistic batching (global queue): rollback to smaller batches under high concurrency.
  * Soft-affinity with TTL (5 minutes): preferential routing to last worker but allow overflow batching elsewhere.
  * Strict-affinity (session pinned until end): KV cache warm and retained, no cross-session batching.
- Batching windows: 0ms (opportunistic immediate), 10ms, 50ms, 200ms.
- KV cache: simulated hit rates derived from session length + affinity: no-affinity ~ 6% hit, soft ~ 36% hit, strict ~ 88% hit on long-chat token reuse.

Key aggregated results (selected metrics):
- Metric definitions: median_latency = median end-to-end per-token latency (ms), p95_latency = 95th percentile per-token latency (ms), cost_per_1k_sessions = cloud GPU + amortized infra cost for running the workload for 1k sessions (USD).

Table (text format) — representative rows (note: these are consolidated averages across model variants; later sections break down by model):

Policy | Batching window | p95_latency (ms) | median_latency (ms) | kv_hit_rate (%) | cost_per_1k_sessions (USD)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No-affinity | 0ms        | 240            | 80               | 6    | $2,940
Soft-affinity | 10ms     | 160            | 72               | 38   | $2,420
Soft-affinity | 50ms     | 140            | 68               | 41   | $2,150
Strict-affinity | 0ms    | 120            | 64               | 86   | $3,050
Strict-affinity | 200ms   | 200            | 82               | 88   | $2,980

Observations from table:
- Strict affinity yields the best KV hit rate and lowest median latency for long chats, but its lack of cross-session batching raises overall cost in the baseline 0ms batching case (more workers needed to maintain peak QPS).
- Soft-affinity with a 50ms batch window is a sweet spot: it recovers much of the KV benefit while preserving enough batching to lower per-session cost versus strict-affinity.
- Very large batching windows (200ms) hurt p95 latency on short chats even if they reduce cost slightly; user-perceived interactivity degrades.

Model-specific snapshots (not exhaustive) — redwood-14B-int8 vs redwood-7B-fp16:
- redwood-14B-int8: per-token compute is ~1.7x redwood-7B-fp16 in these builds, but quality-sensitive workloads prefer 14B. With strict affinity, the higher KV hit rate reduces extra tokens computed and narrows cost gap (cost_per_1k_sessions for strict-affinity drops ~12% vs no-affinity).
- redwood-7B-fp16: cheaper per-token but benefits less from KV reuse (smaller KV entry payloads). In opportunistic batching, 7B has stronger cost advantage.

ASCII sparkline: relative cost per 1k sessions (lower is better) across policies (index normalized to No-affinity 0ms = 100):
No-affinity   : [=====100=====]
Soft-affinity : [===  82   ===]
Soft-affinity(50ms): [==  73  ==]
Strict-affinity  : [====110====]

Per-session amortization note (how we computed cost_per_1k_sessions):
- Sum of GPU runtime cost + NVMe spinning for KV (small) + amortized instance baselines + networking egress estimate.
- Allocated workers scaled to meet p95 latency target under the policy; auto-scaler profile used same cooldown/scale step for fair comparison.

Tail-latency breakouts (p99 insight):
- No-affinity & small windows: p99 spikes due to model contention when many sessions spuriously align; spikes correlated with microburst clocks in the synthetic generator.
- Soft-affinity mitigates these spikes by allowing warm-KV reuse while still sending overflow to other workers. p99 reductions of 28–42% vs no-affinity in our runs.

Tradeoffs / recommended routing defaults for Console: (draft proposals)
1) Default: Soft-affinity with 50ms batching window + TTL 5m. Rationale: balance KV hit gains (~40%) with batching efficiency and maintain p95 latency within SLA for interactive apps.
2) For latency-sensitive short-turn experiences (e.g., instant completion widgets): reduce window to 10ms and lower TTL to 1m to increase cross-session batching while accepting lower KV benefit.
3) For long-conversation assistants with high token reuse (support bots): allow strict-affinity toggle in Dedicated / Private with explicit cost visibility and autoscaler tuning guidance.

Operational notes for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private:
- Dedicated: predictable worker pool makes strict-affinity economically palatable; include a recommended reservation plan in the UI explaining the cost delta.
- Hosted: recommend soft-affinity default; strict-affinity should be gated behind a feature flag with billing warnings.
- Private: behave like Dedicated but include HSM/KMS notes in the deployment guide (KV persistence encryption).

Open questions / next experiments (actionable):
- Sweep: affinity TTL values {30s, 1m, 5m, 15m} combined with windows {0,10,50,100}ms to map a full Pareto frontier (priority: run on H100 private cluster).
- Real traffic replay: run against anonymized customer sessions to validate hit-rate models (we used synthetic reuse heuristics).
- Quantization sensitivity: run 3-level quant (int4, int8, fp16) under affinity policies — initial runs show int4 amplifies latency volatility under high microburst.
- Cost model refinement: include per-IOPS NVMe cost and different cloud egress tiers per region.

Appendix A — short trace sample (one long chat, strict-affinity, redwood-14B-int8):
- Session start (t=0): cold model init = +450ms overhead (amortized across session in strict-affinity).
- Turn 1 token loop: median token latency 52ms.
- Turn 12 token loop (KV warm): median token latency 34ms, KV reuse reducing compute by ~28% for repeated prefixes.
- End-to-end session total tokens: 1,800; total additional compute saved from KV ~520 tokens equivalent.

Appendix B — immediate TODOs for this doc:
- Run the affinity TTL sweep on H100 private cluster (assigned to Marcus).
- Add a cost-per-region breakout for EU vs US (Elena).
- Draft Console wording for the soft-affinity default with toggles and a small explainer tooltip (Samir).

Notes / provenance:
- Synthetic generator: scripts/perf/sim_session_mixer_v2 (see linked github).
- Cost numbers include reserved instance discounts where applicable for Dedicated runs — exact reservation delta documented in separate spreadsheet (link in confluence).

If you review this and want a short slide deck for internal sync (10m), I can produce a 6-slide deck summarizing the sweet spots and recommended Console defaults.

-- Priya
